usage.notes: Use GDC open metadata/data for targeted cancer-genomics research and reproducible curated snapshots. Treat controlled-access files as a separate protected data class requiring explicit dbGaP/eRA authorization and purpose-limited handling. Do not bulk-fetch genomic files into the browser. Large files should be handled by authorized server-side workflows or approved research pipelines; the web UI should receive only the minimum normalized metadata/results needed for the current feature.

license.identifier: NIH/NCI GDC data access policies and source-program terms
license.scope: GDC contains both open-access and controlled-access data. Controlled access is determined by participant consent and program data-access policies and requires appropriate dbGaP authorization/eRA authentication. Study/program-specific publication, redistribution and acknowledgement requirements can also apply. Review the exact project/file access class and governing policy before commercial or production reuse.
license.notes: Access permission is not a content license and must not be broadened by Panacea. Preserve program/project attribution and any source-study acknowledgements. Do not redistribute controlled data or derived information beyond the user's approved research purpose and authorization.

validation.notes: GDC provides harmonized and curated cancer research data but is not a direct patient-care diagnostic service. Cohort data, genomic pipelines and clinical metadata may be valuable for research/education, yet individual treatment decisions require separately validated clinical assays, pathology context and clinical evidence.

provenance.authority: National Cancer Institute / Genomic Data Commons
provenance.notes: Persist GDC API/status version, project/program IDs, entity UUIDs, case/sample/aliquot identifiers as supplied by GDC, data category/type, experimental strategy, workflow/pipeline metadata, reference genome/assembly where relevant, file UUID/name/format/size/checksum, open-versus-controlled access class, release/retrieval date and Panacea adapter version. Derived analyses must retain the exact source file/entity UUIDs and processing versions.

adapter.notes: Planned flow for open data: explicit project/cohort query -> GDC API metadata search -> validate UUIDs/access class -> retrieve only required open records/files -> normalize metadata and research observations to PanaceaCancerGenomicDataset. Controlled-data flow must be implemented separately behind server-side authorization, encrypted storage, audit logging and purpose checks; never place GDC authentication tokens in browser code, localStorage, URLs or logs. Token-bearing requests must fail closed on authorization mismatch or expired access.

trust.notes: Highly authoritative NCI cancer-genomics resource with stable UUIDs, documented harmonization pipelines and strong reproducibility when source files/workflows are pinned. Access/redistribution rights vary by project and open-versus-controlled status, so rights cannot be represented by one permissive blanket license.
